ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $O$ is the intersection point of the diagonals of rectangle $ABCD$, $DE \parallel AC$, $CE \parallel BD$, and $DE$ intersects $CE$ at point $E$. Given that $AB=4$ and $AD=6$, what is the perimeter of quadrilateral $OCED$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle,\\
it follows that $\angle BAD=90^\circ$, OB=OD=OC=OA,\\
thus BD= $\sqrt{AB^{2}+AD^{2}}= 2\sqrt{13}$,\\
since OD= $\frac{1}{2}$BD= $\sqrt{13}$,\\
and DE$\parallel$ AC, CE$\parallel$ BD,\\
it follows that quadrilateral OCED is a parallelogram,\\
since OC=OD,\\
thus quadrilateral OCED is a rhombus,\\
hence the perimeter of quadrilateral OCED $=4$OD$= 4\sqrt{13}=\boxed{4\sqrt{13}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, ABCD is a rectangle, A and B are on the left side, upper and lower, D and C are on the right side, upper and lower; diagonals AC and BD intersect at O inside the rectangle; the point E on the right side is formed by the intersection of the line segment DE passing through D and the line segment CE passing through C, and the diagram corresponds to DE ∥ AC, CE ∥ BD. Then reason: Because O and C are on diagonal AC, OC is a part of AC; and DE ∥ AC, so DE ∥ OC. Because O and D are on diagonal BD, OD is a part of BD; and CE ∥ BD, so CE ∥ OD. Therefore the two pairs of opposite sides of quadrilateral OCED are respectively parallel, so it is a parallelogram. The two diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so OC and OD are both halves of the rectangle's diagonals, and OC = OD. Thus parallelogram OCED has one pair of adjacent sides equal, so it is a rhombus. The rectangle diagonal BD = √(AB² + AD²) = √(4² + 6²) = √52 = 2√13, so OD = BD/2 = √13. The perimeter of rhombus OCED is 4 × √13 = 4√13.
